models.purpose: Fold four layers of adjacency into one goal-to-goal matrix.
models.summary: Data series are linked when their Pearson correlation exceeds 0.9 at a significance below 0.1, giving the data adjacency. That matrix is carried up through the indicator, target and goal layers by products with the cross-layer adjacencies fixed by the official structure, so the goal matrix is a seven-factor product.

variables.definition: adjacency among the 500 data series, set by correlation
links from indicators to data series, fixed by the official structure

governing_equations.label: Aii
governing_equations.purpose: lift the data links to the indicator layer

governing_equations.label: Att
governing_equations.source_expression: A_tt = A_ti · A_id · A_dd · A_di · A_it
governing_equations.purpose: lift the data links to the target layer

governing_equations.label: Agg
governing_equations.source_expression: A_gg = A_gt · A_ti · A_id · A_dd · A_di · A_it · A_tg
governing_equations.normalized_latex: A_{gg}=A_{gt}\cdot A_{ti}\cdot A_{id}\cdot A_{dd}\cdot A_{di}\cdot A_{it}\cdot A_{tg}
governing_equations.purpose: lift the data links to the goal layer

equation_status.reason: the three products were read from the page raster

objectives: let the data, not expert judgement, set the goal-to-goal ties
constraints: a data link is kept only when the correlation exceeds 0.9 and the significance is below 0.1

details: the matrix is built once from the whole window
the correlation cutoff and the significance cutoff bound which data links exist

parameter_estimation.method: pearson correlation with a stated cutoff and significance level

steps: multiply up through the three layers

assumptions: the influence between two targets is symmetric

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: the goal network is drawn for ten regions

validation_refs: section 3.2 reads the sign and size of the entries for the world region
models.computational_cost: one correlation matrix over 500 series, then three matrix products
strengths: the goal ties come from data rather than from expert opinion
limitations: the cutoff of 0.9 drops most pairs
the product treats every layer as equally reliable
missing_details: no count is given of how many data pairs survive the cutoff
the pearson formula itself is not written

models.purpose: Score each goal by how far its development pushes the others.
models.summary: Implementation levels sit in a vector between zero and one. One step of influence is the adjacency times that vector, and the paper insists on the matrix power rather than the scalar multiple so that indirect chains are counted. The score of developing one goal is the one-norm of a high power of the adjacency.

variables.definition: seventeen implementation levels, each between 0 and 1
the goal adjacency, with entries clipped to the unit interval
number of steps, read as years

governing_equations.label: xn
governing_equations.source_expression: x_n = A^n x_0, not A·(n x_0)
governing_equations.purpose: count indirect chains by powering the matrix

governing_equations.label: y
governing_equations.purpose: score the long-run effect of developing one goal

equation_status.reason: all three were read from the page rasters

objectives: rank goals by their total downstream effect
count indirect paths, not only direct edges
constraints: matrix entries above 1 are clipped to 1 and entries below 0 are clipped to 0

details: the starting vector is the current implementation level
every entry of the result is kept inside 0 to 1 by the clipping
a large n is said to stand for the long run, but no limit is derived

parameter_estimation.method: n is set to 10 for the decade forecast and left large otherwise

steps: raise it to the nth power
take the one-norm as the score
algorithm.convergence_criteria: not stated; n is chosen rather than tested for convergence

assumptions: the ties stay fixed over time
a goal's development feeds back on itself

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: scores are computed for ten regions and the decade forecast names how many regions reach each goal

validation_refs: section 4.3 says the regional priorities agree with reality
models.computational_cost: one matrix power per region on a 17 by 17 matrix
strengths: the same score is comparable across regions
limitations: clipping the entries to 0 and 1 erases the negative ties the network was built to show
the one-norm of a power is not the same object as the powered vector
missing_details: the value of n used for the printed scores is not stated
no test is given that the power has settled

models.section: 6.1 Impact on Network Model and Priority Selection
models.purpose: Rewrite the goal network after a crisis or an opportunity.
models.summary: Without a shock the state moves by the network; with a shock it moves by a new network. The gap between the two states is a perturbation, and cancelling the starting state gives the new network as the old one plus a correction. The correction is also written as a resistance coefficient times the perturbation, and the two writings do not agree.

variables.definition: implementation vector after the network acts, with no shock
disturbance the event adds to each goal
coefficient said to measure how hard the region resists the event

governing_equations.purpose: move the state with no shock
move the state with the shock
tie the two states by the perturbation

governing_equations.label: ΔG
governing_equations.source_expression: G' = G + ΔG, ΔG = c · Δx
governing_equations.purpose: rewrite the correction through a resistance coefficient

equation_status.reason: equations (1) to (5) and the resistance form were read from the page rasters

objectives: show how one event moves the priority order
keep the same scoring method on the new network
constraints: the starting state is assumed invertible

details: the starting state is the current implementation level
the rewrite is a single step

parameter_estimation.method: the perturbation entries are set by hand from common sense, for instance war on the first goal at -0.8

steps: set the perturbation for the event

assumptions: the starting state has an inverse
the effect of an event can be written as one additive vector

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: six perturbation vectors are printed and one region is worked through, but the resistance coefficient is never given a value

validation_refs: section 6.2 compares priorities before and after a natural disaster
models.computational_cost: one matrix correction and one rescore per event
strengths: the shock enters as one named correction, so the before and after can be compared
six events are written out in full
limitations: equation (5) corrects by the inverse times the perturbation while the later line corrects by a coefficient times the perturbation, and the two cannot both hold
a 1 by 17 state is treated as an invertible matrix
missing_details: the resistance coefficient has no printed value
no rule turns an event into its perturbation entries

dependency_edges.handoff: the goal adjacency is the influence matrix that gets powered
the goal adjacency is the network the shock corrects
the corrected network is rescored by the same one-norm
